items.author: Claude (found by the BL-1033 lane on 2026-09-17, flagged by its cold review; filed by the main session)
items.title: A copied world does not tick byte for byte as its original: find the unfaithful copy and make world copies exact
items.design:
DELIVERED 2026-09-18 (sprint 45). Commit 1c5d60b1, merged d61b6ae8. MSVC's unordered_map copy re-inserts in source order and puts each key at the FRONT of its bucket, so every multi-key bucket came out reversed; body_mean_habitability sums floats in population_centres order, so a copy's wages moved two ULP in tick 0's budget lap. world's unordered stores (and province_partition::tile_province) are now faithful_unordered_map, whose copy iterates in its source's order and throws if it cannot. MAIN-SESSION EVIDENCE on 26c8ec6e: world_copy_determinism --seed 28 PASS copied at base, at land and by assignment (D_settle 265C48A23E313B1A both sides); world_determinism ALL PASS on 26c8ec6e, digests 099530C9B7A211D7 / 3C348D569EEF30EB / 583A788BD8045DA0 / 2EC67DAE697FBA02 unchanged. landscape_search_harness PASS (R2 thread invariance at 2/3/4/8 threads, R3 path replay); player_seed_sweep --digest-check on the integrated main 26c8ec6e (BL-1034, BL-1036, BL-1037, BL-1038 and its fix round): 16/16 rows PASS against the BL-1031 pins, 0 threw, 4289 s (machine contended) — main session, 2026-09-18. Lane run: --seeds all 16/16 (5551 s, contended). COLD REVIEW: no correctness bug; the fix leaves the order dependence in place — a saved-and-loaded world still diverges, and five readers let hash order reach arithmetic — so BL-1050 (order-dependent reads) carries it, riding this sprint's re-bless (NR-894).

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM ---

SCHEDULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-890): early in sprint 45, ahead of Beat 1 — Beat 1 and the wizard's time-lapse round are the likeliest first features to copy a world and tick it.

FOUND 2026-09-17 by the BL-1033 lane (charter budget cost), probing whether one pre-landscape world per seed could be copied per matrix row. On seed 28 a copied base world matched the BL-1031 pins at D_search and D_land, but after the 12-tick validation settle it digested D_settle 18F78EB9B2B20F29 against the pinned 265C48A23E313B1A — whether copied before the landscape or after it — while the original world, settled with a copied recipe_registry, matches the pin. So `world`'s copy is faithful as data and unfaithful as a program: something the tick path reads differs between an original and its copy. Suspected (not located): an unordered container whose iteration order depends on insertion/rehash history, a pointer-keyed cache, or a cache the copy constructor carries stale.

WHY IT MATTERS. The simulation is deterministic by standing rule. The landscape search copies the base world for every evaluation (landscape_search.cpp score_one) but only scores statically, so today's shipped worlds are unaffected; any future feature or instrument that copies a world and then ticks it (a what-if preview, a save-branch, a matrix instrument) silently diverges. The harness comment in tools/verify/harness_params.hpp above build_app_base_world is the only other record.

THE WORK. A minimal reproduction in a harness (build seed 28 in app order, copy, settle both, compare snapshot bytes per tick to find the first tick that diverges), then bisect the tick path to the reading that differs, then fix the copy (or the container) so a copy ticks byte for byte. DONE WHEN: the reproduction passes on the 16 library seeds with the BL-1031 pins unmoved; if the fix must change iteration order on the ORIGINAL path, that is a world-mover and needs Ben's re-bless authorisation first.

items.title: A span resumed from a handoff struct carries its dated objects, keeps its 1200 anchors explicitly, and proves it under a fidelity check
items.design:
DELIVERED 2026-09-18 (sprint 45). Commit 9bc4eadf, merged 614a02e5; cold-review follow-ups 58193812. A resumed span carries dated objects, civilisations and universal creeds; consolidation and the near-home cutoff read explicit params anchored at 1200; only living polities are noted as founded at a resumed open (a visible change to the shipped 1200 replay: dead realms no longer 'rise' in the wizard's Exploration ticker; no digest moves). MAIN-SESSION EVIDENCE: world_determinism ALL PASS on 26c8ec6e, digests 099530C9B7A211D7 / 3C348D569EEF30EB / 583A788BD8045DA0 / 2EC67DAE697FBA02 unchanged. exploration_sim_harness ALL PASS; history_sim_harness at its 2-failure baseline; --fidelity gates 1 and 2 16/16 (divergence to 1960 by source: market stamp up to 808 regions, 1660 record up to 615, dead-filter 0, seed up to 790, residual 0); player_seed_sweep --digest-check on the integrated main 26c8ec6e (BL-1034, BL-1036, BL-1037, BL-1038 and its fix round): 16/16 rows PASS against the BL-1031 pins, 0 threw, 4289 s (machine contended) — main session, 2026-09-18. R6 PARTIAL: Exploration's own 1200 resume still restarts the civilisation and creed tables — BL-1049, held for the continuity pass.

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM ---

WHY (engine read, 2026-09-18, checked). run_history_sim resumes only four tables (resume_polities/grudges/contacts/corridors, history_sim.hpp:1713-1721; copy at history_sim.cpp:1490-1496). exploration_output already holds dated_objects and trade_flows, but a span open drops them, so: every treaty clause and tribute is lost; round 1 re-forms treaties against an EMPTY flow table, which INFLATES pair_trade_value_q (it subtracts only other partners' flows, cpp:1263-1301) and can bind far pairs the history never bound; the re-formed treaties all expire together 80 years later. Consolidation fires on year == params.start_year (cpp:902) and the near-home cutoff reads first.year < params.start_year (cpp:870, :3458, :3519; trace-only :3431, :4446), so a 1660 open would re-sweep every seat's stores into the capital (a second windfall, feeding Beat 1's capital paid in) and reclassify the 1,250 pairs met after 1200 as near-home. out.civilisations and out.universal_creeds start empty on a resume while the region/polity indices into them carry (settlement.hpp:473, :613; history_sim.hpp:2345), so a new record reuses index 0 and a known pair is recorded twice (cpp:3876-3916). A resumed span notes EVERY polity, dead ones included, as founded at its open (cpp:2598-2599).

RULED (DIGITISATION.md, the span paragraphs; PROPOSED 2026-09-18 and not overturned): the span is its own call resumed from exploration_output; consolidation and near-home stay anchored at 1200; trade flows need no pointer of their own, because the round-1 upkeep rebuilds them from dated_objects before any read (cpp:787-791, :1157, :3327 precede :3462).

THE WORK. (1) A resume_dated_objects pointer, copied beside cpp:1493-1496; the Exploration caller leaves it null. (2) consolidation_year and near_home_cutoff_year as explicit history_sim_params, read at every site above; Exploration sets both to empires_stop_year, which is its own start_year, so it is byte-identical. (3) Carry the civilisation and universal-creed tables across a resume (or re-key their indices) — check the digests before calling it non-moving. (4) A resumed span notes only living polities as founded (event layer, record_playback only). (5) A resume-fidelity check in digitisation_sim_harness: resume from the fixture's exploration_handoff at 1660 (rebuild creed_state from cultures; works and terrain from the fixture); GATE that the opening state equals the struct field for field and that after one round treaties, the overlord graph and stocks equal the continued run's 1660 round apart from the named network sources; REPORT the 1960 divergence against --through attributed by source (the 1660 corridor record, the dead-filter, the seed). Never gate it bit for bit — a lossless resume cannot equal the continued run, because a span reads its inherited corridor record until it closes (cpp:3327, :3420, :7312-7352) and the handoff filters corridors over the span's dead (cpp:8483-8493).

DONE WHEN. world_determinism digests unchanged; player_seed_sweep --digest-check holds (16 seeds, or a stated subset while BL-1034 runs); exploration_sim_harness green; history_sim_harness at its tracked 2-failure baseline (R3a2/R3a3); the fidelity check passes on the 16 library seeds and prints its divergence table.

items.title: A resumed span reopens a bought road rung at the tier it was bought to, behind a switch the sprint 45 re-bless turns on
items.design:
DELIVERED 2026-09-18 (sprint 45), SWITCH OFF. Commit 0b956ac5, merged 614a02e5. history_sim_params::resume_seeds_corridor_tier seeds each resumed corridor at its recorded rung, both directions; BL-1044 turns it on with the re-bless. MAIN-SESSION EVIDENCE: --resume-tier 16/16 (switch-on invariants at 1200 and 1660; the cold review calls it a regression guard more than independent evidence); switch off, world_determinism ALL PASS on 26c8ec6e, digests 099530C9B7A211D7 / 3C348D569EEF30EB / 583A788BD8045DA0 / 2EC67DAE697FBA02 unchanged. player_seed_sweep --digest-check on the integrated main 26c8ec6e (BL-1034, BL-1036, BL-1037, BL-1038 and its fix round): 16/16 rows PASS against the BL-1031 pins, 0 threw, 4289 s (machine contended) — main session, 2026-09-18. PREMISE CORRECTED by the lane's per-seed counts: no Empire-bought rung is demoted at 1200 on any library seed; what the switch changes is refused walks promoted at 1200 (2-110 a seed), and post roads demoted at 1660 (12 seeds) and bought a second time (9 seeds).

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM ---

RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): the fix rides sprint 45's one re-bless. This reopens the defect BL-959 (empire corridor upgrade records its uses) closed as a KNOWN UNDER-READ comment on 2026-09-16 (history_sim.cpp:2010-2015).

WHY. A resumed span seeds live road counts from the corridor record's `uses` (cpp:1832-1840), never from its `tier`. A bought rung sets the live count to the tier threshold but records one walk (Empires: cpp:2031 and :2040, supply_upgrade_material_cost 2000 at era_minus_one.cpp:137; a post road: :2066 and :2073), so it reopens at the tier its walks earn — already at 1200 for Empire-bought Tracks and Roads, and at 1660 for post roads. The error runs both ways: a refused walk held one short live but counted in the record resumes promoted (cpp:1979-1989). A post road reopened at tier 2 can be bought a second time (cpp:3388, :2059). Beat 1's rail sink is the rung above the post road, so a demoted post road would misprice it.

THE WORK. Seed each resumed corridor's live count from max(uses, threshold(tier)) and resolve the refused-walk promotion the same way, behind history_sim_params::resume_seeds_corridor_tier (default false). BL-1044 turns it on. Update the KNOWN UNDER-READ comment to say what now holds.

DONE WHEN. Switch off: world_determinism and --digest-check unmoved. Switch on, per library seed: corridors whose resumed tier changed, by span (1200 and 1660), and no corridor reopening below the tier it was bought to; no rung bought twice.

items.title: The charter spend takes a square-root cap under a density ceiling that fills goods in turn, and the cost table gains the rows to set it
items.design:
DELIVERED 2026-09-19 (sprint 45). Round 1 a1b82386 merged 38561e52, fix round 220cab6c, round 2 4be0c877 merged 9f7a0e92. MAIN-SESSION EVIDENCE: the 21 timed rows on a quiet machine (seeds 0/28/46 x 1x/2x/4x x ceilings 120/160, main at ab9c38f8, 7126 s; spend rules and points balance PASS on every row) folded into charter_cost_sweep.json as runs.bl1039_sqrt (4ffc6716); chain 11 on be5b3d72 (main session, 2026-09-19; BL-1042 and its fix round, BL-1059 rounds 1-3 merged): world_determinism ALL PASS, digests 099530C9B7A211D7 / 3C348D569EEF30EB / 583A788BD8045DA0 / 2EC67DAE697FBA02 unchanged; exploration_sweep --out then seed_library --check --from: 0 moved, 0 absent, 16 unchanged; player_seed_sweep --digest-check 16/16 PASS (2959 s); empty, zero and refused digest checks 3/3 on 0/28/46; charter_refusal_probe ALL PASS. The cold review of round 2 found nothing blocking; its design call (a failed placement forfeits the centre, NR-903 -> skip) and low findings went to BL-1060 (charter spend hardening).

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM ---

REVISED (Ben, 2026-09-18, wave 1 form, NR-895): capital REVERTS to the 400 +/-40% draw and the unspent-points rule is removed; the ceiling fills goods in turn; B is net of specialist prices and B_ref = 8 x goods x firm price. Built and merged: round 1 a1b82386 (38561e52), fix round b6425e26 (220cab6c); round 2 in the lane. The timed rows run first thing 2026-09-19 on a quiet machine (Ben).

RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation; DIGITISATION.md § 1, CORPORATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 and Pass 6): the per-resource cap scales by a SQUARE ROOT of the body's charter capital under a named DENSITY CEILING below the 200-per-body guard, with its own unspent reason; a budget specialist's starting capital is its centre's UNSPENT points at a stated rate, in place of the 400 +/-40% draw. PROPOSED: the rate makes one specialist's price in points worth 400 credits.

THE WORK. (1) The budget path reads its OWN restated constants, k_charter_max_firms_per_body = 200 and k_charter_per_resource_firm_cap = 8 (corporation_generation.cpp:2576-2578), whose comment couples them to Pass 6's (:2168-2170). Replace their use (cpp:3091, :3119-3122, :3127-3132) with a rule in charter_spend_params: per-good cap = max(8, floor(8 * sqrt(B / B_ref))), where B_ref is the budget the legacy cap would spend and G (goods with demand on the body) is DEFINED EXPLICITLY and fixed before the walk — upkeep and construction demand are re-measured per firm (cpp:3106-3114), so an undefined G drifts as firms land. Break the Pass 6 coupling; leave cpp:2168-2170 alone. Keep the legacy bool modes selectable so every pinned digest holds. (2) A density ceiling F_max < 200 with unspent reason density_ceiling (enum count at charter_budget.hpp:146, the name switch, the sweep's unspent_reasons). (3) A capital rule in charter_spend_params: specialist capital = centre remainder x rate; the remainder is what the centre could not spend after its specialist and firms; no shipped default (the contract at charter_budget.hpp:73-81 stands: refuse <= 0). capital_params is default-constructed at cpp:2945 today. (4) The report gains firms per good per body, G, seat balance and a solvent flag. (5) Fix the budget_system.hpp:20 comment ('~2%/qtr'; the rate is 1.5%, budget_system.cpp:312-315).

ROWS. Seeds 0, 28, 46 at 1x/2x/4x synthetic: the sqrt rule with ceilings near 120 and 160, per-good tallies on every row, so the table finally holds rows between 81 and 150 firms. About 1-1.5 h at BL-1033's row cost; keep-awake; never copy a world and then tick it (BL-1034). Ends in a NEEDS_REVIEW call for B_ref's definition and the ceiling.

NOT A WORLD-MOVER: nothing under src/ builds a budget (charter_budget.hpp:17-18). DONE WHEN: --digest-check none, empty, zero and refused hold; the synthetic legacy-mode digests hold; the new rows are in charter_cost_sweep.json with their note; the call is filed.

items.title: Beat 1: regions with centres accrue located industry points from 1660 to 1960, from scale, their own fuel, Industry capacity and treasury paid in
items.design:
DELIVERED 2026-09-19 (sprint 45), SWITCH OFF. Commit 8c3b4a1d merged f8137b8d; cold-review fix round 2c6df95f merged 849a358d. MAIN-SESSION EVIDENCE on 849a358d: chain 8 (world_determinism ALL PASS, digests unchanged; seed_library --check 0 moved; --fidelity 16/16; player_seed_sweep --digest-check 16/16 PASS). digitisation_sim_harness --through 1960, 16 worlds: rho(points, urban heads) med 0.839, rho(scale points, head-years) med 0.900, treasury-paid share med 0.690, top-region share med 0.280. RE-RULED 2026-09-19 (NR-896, NR-897, both option A): the Fuel Doctrine pulls read a share and treasury points spread by scale, in BL-1056. Capacity-kind filter: BL-1057.

--- THE ORIGINAL ITEM ---

RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation; DIGITISATION.md § Beat 1): capital is paid in as a CONSEQUENCE — each round a fixed share of the capital treasury's surplus after the round's bills converts to industry points; no polity scores it, so it adds no § 11 verb. This cut carries NO sink (rail, mechanised force and works stay the design and come later, each with its own measurement). PROPOSED, not overturned: the stock sits on each region with centres (the sim has no centre entity: settlement.hpp:526-553); a region's own fuel sets its rate as a soft factor with a floor; ground the sim founded is re-surveyed at 1660; treasury points land on the capital's own region.

THE WORK. (1) An int64 industry_points field on region, credited to the region itself each round (order-independent), inside the Digitisation span only. Rate = urban scale x fuel factor (soft, with a floor) x (1000 + the Industry industrial modifier)/1000. CONTINUITY PASS (Ben, 2026-09-18): held for the continuity pass run after each generation round is done — this one after Digitisation — not built mid-sprint.

THE IDEA (Ben, 2026-09-18, on NR-891's forest ruling): push forest into the culture round. WHY IT MATTERS ONLY AS A STOCK: nothing in Era -1 writes tile cover (the sim sees cover through a read-only sim_terrain_view), so a forest share surveyed at 400 BCE equals one surveyed at 1660 — BL-1051's span-open survey is equivalent while forest is static. Then the 1660 share says whose woods survived, and Charcoal Iron is the answer of the polity that kept them — coke winning where the woods ran out.

The seat menu turns on the divisor over m alone (stage 1: the anchor's 9 seats near a ratio of 160), and firm density on the divisor alone; BL-1044 pins m so the median menu matches the legacy anchor, and the divisor against the tick. items.author: Claude (found running BL-1044's owed ctest pass, 2026-09-22)
items.title: The CTest tier links what its harnesses now use: a family of Debug targets has been unbuildable since the harnesses adopted the app-order build
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-22 running BL-1044's owed ctest pass. `nmake all` stops at the first failing target, so the suite reads as "Not Run" rather than as a broken build, and the breakage hid.

WHAT IS BROKEN. Every harness that builds its world in APP ORDER goes through tools/verify/harness_params.hpp, which includes scripting/lua_state.hpp and calls build_app_base_world — so it needs lua54 AND the Lua TUs the Lua-free world superset excludes (world_gen_config.cpp, works_registry.cpp, recipe_registry.cpp, tech_tree.cpp). The CMake targets name those by hand, one target at a time, and the ones written before harness_params spread do not. Measured tonight, building all 157 CTest targets by name: player_seed_sweep failed on LNK2019 world_gen_config::load_from_lua / works_registry::load_from_lua (fixed at ee7ef3c3, which restored the player_seed_sweep_guard row — the row that now carries the one-player invariant, S7); campaign_lapse, chain_conversion_probe, convoy_cargo_census and others fail on LNK2019 lua_close / luaL_unref, i.e. they do not link lua54 at all. battle_engagement_harness is a separate, older break (a torn-out mercenary symbol, 2026-08-30).

THE WORK. Take the failing list from the overnight build (scratchpad overnight3/build_failures.txt, or rebuild by name to regenerate it); for each, add lua54 and whichever Lua TUs it pulls, or move it onto a shared helper so the list stops being hand-kept — the hand-kept list is the defect, and DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md § A harness must build the world the application builds is what keeps growing it. Then run the suite and record which rows breach the 60 s default now that the span runs by default (BL-1044: the budget row's generation is a median 53.3 s in Release).

DONE WHEN. Every CTest target builds by name, `ctest --test-dir build` runs every row rather than reporting Not Run, and the rows that legitimately exceed 60 s carry a raised timeout with the reason.

THE LIST, measured 2026-09-22 by building all 157 CTest test names (14 stops, three classes). items.title: The player's own construction does not complete on the shipped world: a military base sits unfinished for 100 ticks with 70,000 credits in hand
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-23 running BL-1044's owed visual suite: 11 of the 12 script failures share one cause — scripts/verify/lib.lua's shared UI fixture (`raise_player_force`) cannot stage, because the player's military base never completes.

MEASURED on the shipped verify world (Release, --verify, one script at a time, probes in the session scratchpad): the player corp opens on 460.7 credits with 4 buildings; `military_base` is `tech_locked` at tick 0 and PLACEABLE after 12 econ ticks (the gate opens with time); placed then, the base is NOT complete 100 ticks later, while the corp's balance climbs past 70,000. So it is not cash, not the tech gate and not the fixture's 40-tick bound: construction itself does not proceed. The two candidates are the ones BL-709 made construction depend on — CONSTRUCTION CAPACITY on the body (the charter web at the pinned 650:2 lays a median 65 firms over 148-538 markets, and the provisioning step charters yards only where a centre's turn reaches them) and the MATERIALS the build draws from the market.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE HARNESS. The app's start path lays the same web the verify path now does (NR-909), so this is the world a player is handed: if construction cannot complete, the core loop's first move does not land. The fixture is the messenger, not the subject — and note its error text says 'never completed within 40 ticks', which reads as a slow build rather than a stalled one.

THE WORK. Read which of capacity or materials is empty at the stall (the construction ledger's own rows, or a probe on `body_construction_demand` / the yard provisioning in the charter walk); then either the web must charter a yard where the player stands, or construction must be able to source capacity across a market, or the opening corp must carry enough to build one. Whichever it is, the reading belongs beside NR-913's density finding: a sparse web is the common cause.

DONE WHEN. On every library seed, the seated player can place AND complete a military base from its opening position within the fixture's bound, and scripts/verify/lib.lua stages on a pristine world (it also needs the tech gate's 12 ticks, which the fixture does not currently wait for).
